instruction: There is a Chrome extension package in the Desktop directory that needs to be loaded. Please install it manually in Chrome as an unpacked extension.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Task requires installing the extension from Desktop. Evaluator checks that at least 1 unpacked extension is installed in Chrome (counting extensions with 'path' attribute in preferences).

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic flaw: Evaluator checks for ANY unpacked extension (count >= 1) rather than verifying the SPECIFIC extension from Desktop was installed
False positive risk: If pre-existing unpacked extensions exist in the VM, evaluator will incorrectly pass even if user did nothing
Insufficient specificity: Getter cannot distinguish between the target 'Hello Extension' from Desktop and other unrelated unpacked extensions
Missing verification: No check for extension properties (name, path from Desktop folder, or manifest details) to confirm the correct extension was loaded
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify getter to check for specific extension properties: verify extension name contains 'Hello' or path contains '/home/user/Desktop/'
Alternative approach: Store initial unpacked extension count in config (via initial getter call), then verify count increased by exactly 1
Alternative approach: Check extension manifest.json properties if extension has unique identifiable fields (name, version, description)
Add getter logic to iterate through all unpacked extensions and verify at least one has path starting with '/home/user/Desktop/'
Consider adding better error handling for missing or corrupt Chrome Preferences file
